record.paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Creative Telescoping
record.original_question: Develop a creative telescoping algorithm for functions that satisfy systems of algebraic differential equations. Here the source motivates the class by examples such as exp(y(e^x − 1)), the partition generating function ∏_{n=0}^∞ (1 − x^n)^{-1}, and the Weierstrass ℘-function, all of which satisfy algebraic differential equations but are not necessarily D-finite.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.2 Develop a creative telescoping algorithm applicable to functions satisfying systems of ADEs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A function f of one or several variables is called D-finite if it satisfies a system of linear differential equations with polynomial coefficients whose solution space is finite-dimensional. More generally, f is said to satisfy a system of algebraic differential equations (ADEs) if there exist polynomials P_1, ..., P_r in finitely many variables such that P_i(x_1, ..., x_n, f, ∂f/∂x_1, ..., ∂^α f/∂x^α) = 0 for all multi-indices α appearing, with at least one nontrivial relation in each independent variable. Examples include exp(y(e^x − 1)), the partition generating function ∏_{n≥0}(1 − x^n)^{-1}, and the Weierstrass ℘-function; these satisfy ADEs but are in general not D-finite.

The method of creative telescoping, given an input function F(t, x_1, ..., x_n), seeks operators (a "telescoper" T acting only on t and a "certificate" C) such that T(F) = ∂_{x_1} G_1 + ... + ∂_{x_n} G_n, so that integrating (or summing) F over the x-variables yields a function of t annihilated by T. Existing creative telescoping algorithms cover D-finite, holonomic, hyperexponential, hypergeometric, and algebraic inputs.

Problem: Develop a creative telescoping algorithm that applies to functions specified as solutions of systems of algebraic differential equations (i.e., to ADE-defined functions in the above sense), producing — when it exists — a telescoper for an integral or sum of such a function with respect to chosen variables, together with the associated certificate, and analyze its termination and complexity.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on creative telescoping focuses on D-finite, hyperexponential, hypergeometric, and algebraic inputs (Bostan, Chen, Chyzak, Kauers, Koutschan, van der Hoeven and others), with reduction-based methods being the most recent advance. No published algorithm appears to handle the broader class of functions defined by general systems of algebraic differential equations (which includes non-D-finite examples such as the partition generating function and the Weierstrass ℘-function). The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Constructing reductions for creative telescoping
status_evidence.snippet: Reduction-based algorithms have been extended to more general classes of functions, such as hyperexponential functions, hypergeometric terms, algebraic functions and most recently D-finite functions.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art creative telescoping algorithms cover up to D-finite/algebraic inputs, not general ADE-defined inputs.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Hermite Reduction, Creative Telescoping and Definite Integration of D-Finite Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized Hermite reduction extended to D-finite functions for creative telescoping.
status_evidence.claim: Recent extensions reach D-finite functions; broader ADE class not yet treated.
